situation (example wording): "Carjacking rate in Texas in 2024" (a NIBRS rate for a state or the nation)
what the app does today: State and national NIBRS rates are not built.
proposed behavior: The state or national sum (P61: every month any agency reported) per 100,000 people in the reporting agencies: the sum of the FBI populations of exactly the agencies counted, never weighted by the months reported. Agencies reporting only some months are included and disclosed, as in P61. The consistent-reporters button gives the rate over the agencies that reported every month. P58's every-month rule applies to agency rates, not to state and national sums.
exact default or choices offered: Rate: per 100,000 over the agencies counted (the sentences P15 lists), with P61's disclaimer and button.
why: A rate's population must match its count: the same agencies in both.
status: Decided 2026-10-30 (Jeff: "Agree", on: the rate's population is exactly the agencies counted, no months weighting; then: "state rates in nibrs are relative to the sum of reporting agencies"); the Crime Index population rule for an agency with no value is amended by P184 (cleanup 2026-11-22), audit C11
test cases: Tests that cite this row: scripts/test-nibrs-shadow.ts.
